channel.title: Sublime Pantry
channel.description: Home freeze-drying, batch by batch: machine decisions, troubleshooting, storage, and cottage-business economics.

item.title: The complete batch workflow: from tray prep to sealed mylar
item.description: The full home freeze-drying process done right — prep, cycle stages, the dryness test, and packaging within the window that keeps food crisp for decades.

item.title: Selling freeze-dried food from home: rules, testing, and real unit economics
item.description: What cottage food laws generally allow, the 0.85 water-activity line, sub-$100 testing, labeling — and a worked cost model for pricing a bag of freeze-dried candy.

item.title: Which home freeze dryer should you buy? A decision framework
item.description: A $1,700–$5,000 decision made systematically: size, brand, power, placement, and running cost — with every spec sourced from manufacturer documentation.

item.title: Batch not fully dry in the center trays: causes and fixes
item.description: Why center-tray food comes out cool, flexible, or dark in the middle — and the checks that fix it, in the order to try them.

item.title: Freeze-dried candy came out chewy, melted, or flat: fixes by failure
item.description: Chewy centers, melted puddles, or candy that never puffed — each failure has a distinct cause: spacing, settings, or a candy that fundamentally won't work.

item.title: Food won't rehydrate right: tough, mushy, or bland results
item.description: Rehydration failures trace back to three places: how the food was dried, how it's being rehydrated, and what that food can ever be again. Sorting them out — with the food-safety rule that applies.

item.title: Bags lost their crunch: diagnosing storage failures
item.description: Freeze-dried food that went soft, stale, or off in storage failed at one of five points: dryness, packaging, absorber, seal, or environment. Find yours.

item.title: Vacuum error: finding the leak, fastest checks first
item.description: A vacuum error means the chamber can't reach or hold pressure. Here's the leak hunt in order of likelihood: door gasket, drain valve, hose, then pump.

item.title: Harvest Right vs. Blue Alpine vs. Stay Fresh: the spec comparison
item.description: The three main US home freeze dryer brands compared on price, capacity, power, pump, and warranty — every figure from manufacturer documentation, with access dates.

item.title: Mylar bags vs. mason jars vs. PETE: freeze-dried storage compared
item.description: The three legitimate storage systems for freeze-dried food, compared on barrier quality, cost per unit, resealability, and fitness for selling vs. pantry use.
